Student-facing error label: Wrong preposition after a verb, adjective, or noun
Complete literacy code: PREP-WRONG — Wrong preposition after a verb, adjective, or noun
Student self-check: Check whether the word before the preposition normally requires a fixed preposition, such as interested in, responsible for, or depend on.
Teacher-facing definition: The preposition is incompatible with the governing verb/adjective/noun or intended relation.
Representative correction: look at the stars

Student-facing error label: Wrong singular or plural noun form
Complete literacy code: NOUN-NUMBER — Wrong singular or plural noun form
Student self-check: Check whether the noun should be singular or plural based on its quantity, determiner, and intended meaning.
Teacher-facing definition: Noun number conflicts with quantity, determiner, or intended reference.
Representative correction: nearby planets

Student-facing error label: Unnecessary tense shift in a past narrative
Complete literacy code: TENSE-SHIFT — Unnecessary tense shift in a past narrative
Student self-check: When describing one past sequence, keep the main verbs in a consistent past-time frame unless the time genuinely changes.
Teacher-facing definition: Unmotivated switching between past and present while narrating past events.
Representative correction: I began to become interested

Searchable grammar label: article use: a, an and the
Complete literacy code: ARTICLE-MISSING — Missing a, an, or the
Student self-check: Check every singular countable noun: it normally needs a/an, the, or another determiner.
Teacher-facing definition: A singular count noun or definite noun phrase lacks a/an/the.
Representative correction: have an interest

Student-facing error label: Wrong noun form in a compound noun
Complete literacy code: NOUN-COMPOUND — Wrong noun form in a compound noun
Student self-check: Check whether the first noun is acting as a modifier; English noun modifiers are usually singular, such as data analysis or shoe shop.
Teacher-facing definition: The first noun in a compound or attributive noun phrase has the wrong number/form.
Representative correction: a four-member team

Complete literacy code: SENTENCE-RUNON — Run-on sentence or comma splice
Student self-check: Check whether both sides could be complete sentences; join them with a full stop, semicolon, or a comma plus a conjunction.
Teacher-facing definition: Independent clauses are joined only by a comma or without a boundary.
Representative incorrect example: the whole universe beyond our earth, these different space systems...
Representative correction: the whole universe beyond Earth. These different space systems...

Searchable grammar label: article use: a, an, the and zero article
Complete literacy code: ARTICLE-EXTRA — Unnecessary a, an, or the
Student self-check: Check whether the noun is a generic plural, an uncountable noun, a proper noun, or part of a fixed expression that takes no article.
Teacher-facing definition: An article is used with a generic plural, mass noun, proper noun, or fixed expression that takes zero article.
Representative correction: buy science novels

Student-facing error label: Missing -s after he, she, it, or a singular noun
Complete literacy code: PRESENT-3S-MISSING — Missing -s after he, she, it, or a singular noun
Student self-check: In the present simple, add -s/-es when the subject is he, she, it, or one singular noun.
Teacher-facing definition: A singular third-person present-tense subject takes a base verb instead of the -s form.
Representative correction: It motivated me

Complete literacy code: SV-AGREEMENT — Subject–verb agreement: singular/plural mismatch
Student self-check: Find the grammatical head of the subject, then make the finite verb singular or plural to match it.
Teacher-facing definition: Singular/plural subject and finite verb do not agree, including compound subjects.
Representative incorrect example: these different space systems and the possibility ... has always led
Representative correction: these different space systems and the possibility ... have always led

Complete literacy code: VERB-PARALLEL — Non-parallel verb forms
Student self-check: Verbs joined in the same list or structure should normally use matching forms.
Teacher-facing definition: Coordinated verbs or complements use mismatched forms.
Representative incorrect example: started to take me ... show me
Representative correction: started taking me ... and showing me

Student-facing error label: Missing be or another auxiliary verb
Searchable grammar label: auxiliary verbs and the verb be
Complete literacy code: AUX-MISSING — Missing be or another auxiliary verb
Student self-check: Check whether the predicate needs am/is/are/was/were, do, have, or another helping verb.
Teacher-facing definition: A clause lacks required be/do/have or another auxiliary.
Representative correction: all have been nourishment / all have nourished

Complete literacy code: NOUN-COUNTABILITY — Countable or uncountable noun error
Student self-check: Check whether the noun can be counted in this meaning and whether it can take a plural, a/an, much, or many.
Teacher-facing definition: A mass noun is pluralised or used with an incompatible determiner; or a count noun is treated as mass.
Representative correction: do volunteer work / volunteer

Complete literacy code: PREP-MISSING — Missing preposition
Student self-check: Check whether the verb, adjective, noun, or phrase requires a preposition before its complement.
Teacher-facing definition: A required preposition is omitted.
Representative correction: learning about an AI-related topic

Complete literacy code: INFINITIVE-FORM — Wrong form in a to-infinitive
Student self-check: After infinitive to, use the base verb; also check whether the controlling word requires to or a bare infinitive.
Teacher-facing definition: The verb after to is not in the base form, or required to is missing/extra.
Representative correction: We have to analyse situations differently

Student-facing error label: Wrong object or complement pattern after a verb
Complete literacy code: VERB-PATTERN — Wrong object or complement pattern after a verb
Student self-check: Check how many objects or complements the verb can take and whether it requires a direct object, preposition, clause, or infinitive.
Teacher-facing definition: A verb is used with the wrong number or type of objects/complements, including an intransitive verb used transitively.
Representative correction: captured/fuelled my imagination

Student-facing error label: Sentence fragment with no finite verb
Complete literacy code: FRAGMENT-NO-VERB — Sentence fragment with no finite verb
Student self-check: A complete sentence needs a finite verb that carries tense or agrees with its subject.
Teacher-facing definition: A phrase/list/reduced clause is presented as a complete sentence without a finite predicate.
Representative incorrect example: Also the process of making rockets, the different strategy of powering them.
Representative correction: I was also fascinated by the process of making rockets and the different strategies used to power them.

Student-facing error label: Incorrect that-clause or wh-clause after a verb
Complete literacy code: CONTENT-CLAUSE — Incorrect that-clause or wh-clause after a verb
Student self-check: Check the clause pattern required after verbs such as know, realise, explain, ask, and understand.
Teacher-facing definition: A reporting or cognition verb takes a malformed content clause.
Representative incorrect example: I learnt that in the different market systems.
Representative correction: I learnt that different market systems require different analyses.

Student-facing error label: Wrong preposition for time, place, or movement
Searchable grammar label: prepositions of time, place and movement
Complete literacy code: PREP-TIME-PLACE — Wrong preposition for time, place, or movement
Student self-check: Choose in, on, at, to, into, from, or another preposition according to the precise time, location, or direction.
Teacher-facing definition: in/on/at/to/into etc. is wrong in a temporal or locative phrase.
Representative correction: During middle school

Student-facing error label: Determiner and noun do not agree
Complete literacy code: DETERMINER-AGREEMENT — Determiner and noun do not agree
Student self-check: Match determiners such as this/these, each/every, much/many, and one of with the correct noun number and countability.
Teacher-facing definition: this/these, every, each, much/many, a lot of, one of, etc. conflict with noun number/countability.
Representative correction: this basic information

Student-facing error label: Wrong gerund or infinitive after a word
Complete literacy code: GERUND-INFINITIVE — Wrong gerund or infinitive after a word
Student self-check: Check the pattern required by the controlling verb or adjective: verb-ing, to + base verb, or a bare infinitive.
Teacher-facing definition: A controlling verb/adjective requires a gerund or infinitive but the wrong complement form is used.
Representative correction: used to look

Student-facing error label: Wrong choice of a, an, the, or no article
Searchable grammar label: article use: a, an, the and zero article
Complete literacy code: ARTICLE-CHOICE — Wrong choice of a, an, the, or no article
Student self-check: Decide whether the noun is first-mentioned, one of many, already known, unique, generic, uncountable, or a proper noun.
Teacher-facing definition: a/an/the/zero article is selected incorrectly.
Representative correction: my father is an expert

Complete literacy code: TENSE-SEQUENCE — Incorrect tense sequence between clauses
Student self-check: Compare the times of the linked clauses and make the tense relationship logically consistent.
Teacher-facing definition: Reported thought/speech or linked clauses use incompatible tense sequencing.
Representative incorrect example: I will take over ... so ... it pushed me
Representative correction: I will take over ... so this pushes/has pushed me

Complete literacy code: PREP-EXTRA — Unnecessary preposition
Student self-check: Check whether the verb takes a direct object without a preposition or whether the expression normally uses no preposition.
Teacher-facing definition: A preposition is inserted where the construction takes a direct object or zero preposition.
Representative incorrect example: discuss with them about how to manage
Representative correction: discuss with them how to manage / discuss management with them

Complete literacy code: POSSESSIVE-FORM — Incorrect possessive form
Student self-check: Check whether possession needs apostrophe-s, a possessive pronoun, or an of-phrase.
Teacher-facing definition: Apostrophe-s, possessive pronoun, or of-genitive is formed incorrectly.
Representative correction: as my university major / as my major at university

Complete literacy code: FUSED-PATTERNS — Two sentence patterns mixed together
Student self-check: Identify the two competing structures and rewrite the sentence using only one complete grammatical pattern.
Teacher-facing definition: Two alternative clause patterns are blended into one ungrammatical construction.
Representative incorrect example: like my favorite book, three body, has a massive plot field
Representative correction: my favourite book, The Three-Body Problem, has a massive plot

Complete literacy code: PASSIVE-FORM — Incorrect passive-voice form
Student self-check: Passive voice normally uses the correct form of be plus a past participle.
Teacher-facing definition: Passive meaning lacks be + past participle or uses the wrong participle/preposition.
Representative correction: Newton's laws learned in Physics 1

Complete literacy code: PAST-PARTICIPLE — Incorrect past participle form
Student self-check: After have or in a passive construction, use the correct past participle, such as written, chosen, or broken.
Teacher-facing definition: Wrong participle after have/be or in a reduced passive construction.
Representative correction: have shown

Complete literacy code: RELATIVE-CLAUSE — Incorrect relative-clause structure
Student self-check: After who/which/that, do not add an extra subject or object when the relative word already fills that role.
Teacher-facing definition: The relative clause has an extra/missing subject, resumptive pronoun, or incompatible structure.
Representative incorrect example: girl that I have many friends
Representative correction: girl who has many friends

Complete literacy code: FRAGMENT-DEPENDENT — Dependent-clause fragment
Student self-check: A clause beginning with because, although, if, when, or another subordinator usually needs a main clause.
Teacher-facing definition: A subordinated because/if/although/when clause is punctuated as a complete sentence.
Representative incorrect example: although the ability to investigate is very important.
Representative correction: Although investigative ability is important, management is also important...

Complete literacy code: PARALLEL-STRUCTURE — Non-parallel list or paired structure
Student self-check: Make items in a list or paired construction use the same grammatical form and function.
Teacher-facing definition: Items in a list/correlative construction have inconsistent grammatical forms.
Representative incorrect example: connected not only to the nearby planet, but also about the whole universe
Representative correction: connected not only to nearby planets but also to the whole universe

Complete literacy code: PERFECT-ASPECT — Incorrect present or past perfect
Student self-check: Use have/has/had + past participle only when the event's relationship to another time requires the perfect aspect.
Teacher-facing definition: Present/past perfect is used incorrectly or omitted where the temporal relation requires it.
Representative incorrect example: Thousands of years ago, ancient people have already had
Representative correction: Thousands of years ago, ancient people already had

Complete literacy code: QUESTION-FORM — Incorrect question word order
Student self-check: Direct questions usually invert the subject and auxiliary; embedded questions use statement word order.
Teacher-facing definition: Direct question lacks subject–auxiliary inversion or required auxiliary.
Representative correction: imagine how far they are

Student-facing error label: Wrong verb form after a preposition
Complete literacy code: VERB-AFTER-PREP — Wrong verb form after a preposition
Student self-check: A verb following a preposition normally takes the -ing form.
Teacher-facing definition: A preposition is followed by a finite/base verb instead of a gerund/noun phrase.
Representative correction: by creating

Student-facing error label: Wrong word form or part of speech
Searchable grammar label: word forms and parts of speech
Complete literacy code: WORD-CLASS — Wrong word form or part of speech
Student self-check: Check whether this position requires a noun, verb, adjective or adverb, and use the correct derived form of the word.
Teacher-facing definition: A related word is used in the wrong grammatical category or derived form, such as a noun where a verb is required or an adjective where a noun is required.
Representative correction: choosing finance or economics

Complete literacy code: ADJECTIVE-COMPLEMENT — Incorrect adjective complement or predicate
Student self-check: Check whether the adjective fits the subject and whether it needs be, a preposition, or a following clause/infinitive.
Teacher-facing definition: Adjective is used with an unsuitable subject or missing complement/copula.
Representative correction: I was very confused

Complete literacy code: CONJUNCTION — Missing or wrong conjunction
Student self-check: Choose a conjunction that expresses the intended relationship and makes the linked clauses or phrases structurally complete.
Teacher-facing definition: Clauses or phrases are linked with an absent or unsuitable conjunction.
Representative incorrect example: Even it was hard for them to learn by themselves
Representative correction: Even though it was hard for them to learn by themselves

Complete literacy code: DETERMINER-EXTRA — Unnecessary or incompatible determiner
Student self-check: Remove a determiner when another determiner already fills the slot or when the noun phrase does not allow it.
Teacher-facing definition: A determiner is redundant or incompatible with the noun phrase.
Representative correction: the experience

Complete literacy code: DETERMINER-MISSING — Missing determiner before a noun
Student self-check: Check whether the noun needs my/your, this/that, some, each, another, or another determiner.
Teacher-facing definition: A noun phrase requires a possessive, demonstrative, quantifier, or article-like determiner.
Representative correction: After quite a long period of thought

Complete literacy code: PRONOUN-CASE — Wrong pronoun form: I/me/my/mine, etc.
Student self-check: Choose the pronoun form according to its job as subject, object, possessive, or reflexive.
Teacher-facing definition: Subject/object/possessive/reflexive pronoun form is wrong.
Representative correction: a hard thing for me

Complete literacy code: PRONOUN-MISSING — Missing pronoun or required subject/object
Student self-check: Check whether every finite clause has a subject and whether the verb or preposition requires an object.
Teacher-facing definition: A required subject, object, or possessive pronoun is omitted.
Representative correction: everyone would look at me

Student-facing error label: Adjective used instead of an adverb, or the reverse
Complete literacy code: ADJ-ADV-FORM — Adjective used instead of an adverb, or the reverse
Student self-check: Use an adjective to describe a noun or subject complement and an adverb to modify a verb, adjective, or other adverb.
Teacher-facing definition: An adjective is used for an adverbial function or vice versa.
Representative correction: in a quick way / quickly

Complete literacy code: ED-ING-ADJECTIVE — Confusion between -ed and -ing adjectives
Student self-check: Use -ing for the thing that causes a feeling and -ed for the person or thing experiencing it.
Teacher-facing definition: Participial adjective has the wrong active/passive meaning.
Representative correction: the field I am interested in / my field of interest

Complete literacy code: PRONOUN-REFERENCE — Unclear or illogical pronoun reference
Student self-check: Make sure the pronoun points clearly to one logical noun and cannot be misread.
Teacher-facing definition: Pronoun does not clearly or logically refer to an antecedent.
Representative correction: check whether my decision is correct

Complete literacy code: COMPARISON-FORM — Incorrect comparative or superlative form
Student self-check: Use the correct -er/-est or more/most form and the correct than or as...as structure.
Teacher-facing definition: Comparative/superlative morphology or than/as structure is incorrect.
Representative correction: When I was even older

Complete literacy code: DANGLING-MODIFIER — Dangling or misattached modifier
Student self-check: The noun immediately after an introductory modifier should be the person or thing performing that modifier's action.
Teacher-facing definition: An introductory or participial modifier attaches to the wrong grammatical subject.
Representative incorrect example: Being a leader, the most important thing was
Representative correction: As a leader, I found that the most important thing was

Complete literacy code: FINITE-VERB — Clause needs a finite verb
Student self-check: A main clause needs a verb marked for tense or modality, not only an -ing or participle phrase.
Teacher-facing definition: A gerund/participle phrase is used where the clause needs a finite verb.
Representative incorrect example: the tree of science grow in my heart
Representative correction: the tree of science growing in my heart

Complete literacy code: NOUN-PHRASE — Incorrect noun-phrase structure
Student self-check: Identify the head noun, then arrange determiners, possessives, adjectives, and noun modifiers around it without duplication.
Teacher-facing definition: The internal structure of a noun phrase is fused, redundant or arranged in a non-grammatical pattern.
Representative incorrect example: the summer institution by the team of Cambridge
Representative correction: a summer programme run by a Cambridge team

Student-facing error label: Unnecessary be or another auxiliary verb
Complete literacy code: AUX-EXTRA — Unnecessary be or another auxiliary verb
Student self-check: Check whether an extra helping verb has created two competing finite verb forms.
Teacher-facing definition: An extra be/do/have produces a double-verb or malformed predicate.
Representative incorrect example: will not have just have one situation
Representative correction: will not have just one situation

Complete literacy code: DOUBLE-LINKER — Double linker: because...so or although...but
Student self-check: Use one linker for the relationship: because without so, or although/even though without but.
Teacher-facing definition: Because...so, although...but, even though...but, etc. redundantly mark the same relation.
Representative incorrect example: Because none of us ... , so we had to
Representative correction: Because none of us ..., we had to / None of us ..., so we had to

Complete literacy code: MODAL-FORM — Incorrect modal-verb construction
Student self-check: After a modal such as can, could, must, should, or may, use the base verb without to or -s.
Teacher-facing definition: Modal meaning/form is incorrect, including mustn't scare, can not caught, etc.
Representative incorrect example: I could both trained ... and reviewed
Representative correction: I could both train ... and review

Complete literacy code: RELATIVE-PRONOUN — Wrong or missing relative pronoun
Student self-check: Choose the relative word according to the antecedent and its role inside the relative clause.
Teacher-facing definition: who/which/that/where/what is missing or incorrectly selected.
Representative correction: a man who was very poor

Student-facing error label: Verb tense conflicts with the time expression
Complete literacy code: TENSE-TIME — Verb tense conflicts with the time expression
Student self-check: Match the verb tense to explicit time words and the actual timing of the event.
Teacher-facing definition: Verb tense does not match an explicit time expression or temporal context.
Representative incorrect example: During my free time, i always go ... At that time, i do
Representative correction: During my free time, I often went ... At that time, I acted

Complete literacy code: IT-THERE-PATTERN — Incorrect it/there sentence pattern
Student self-check: Check whether the sentence needs existential there, anticipatory it, or an ordinary referential subject.
Teacher-facing definition: Extraposition, existential there, or anticipatory it is malformed.
Representative incorrect example: It is very lucky that two people came
Representative correction: I was very lucky that two people came

Complete literacy code: PAST-FORM — Incorrect simple-past verb form
Student self-check: Use the standard past form, especially for irregular verbs such as fell, broke, wrote, and chose.
Teacher-facing definition: Wrong or non-standard simple-past morphology.
Representative correction: This led me

Complete literacy code: PRESENT-3S-EXTRA — Unnecessary -s on a present-tense verb
Student self-check: Do not add -s when the present-simple subject is I, you, we, they, or plural.
Teacher-facing definition: A plural/non-third-person subject is followed by an -s verb.
Representative correction: I studied several subjects

Student-facing error label: Incorrect tense in an if/when future condition
Complete literacy code: CONDITIONAL-TENSE — Incorrect tense in an if/when future condition
Student self-check: Match the tense and modal forms to the intended real, hypothetical, or past-unreal condition.
Teacher-facing definition: Tense or modal in an if/when clause does not match the intended conditional/future meaning.
Representative incorrect example: if we focused ... we will negotiate the price
Representative correction: if we focused ... we would have to adjust the price

Student-facing error label: Wrong verb form after make, let, or help
Searchable grammar label: make, let and help verb patterns
Complete literacy code: MAKE-LET-HELP — Wrong verb form after make, let, or help
Student self-check: Make and let normally take object + base verb; help can take object + base verb or to-infinitive.
Teacher-facing definition: Make, let or help is followed by an incorrect object/complement or non-base verb form.
Representative correction: making me more familiar

Student-facing error label: Incorrect clause after be, seem, think, or a similar expression
Complete literacy code: PREDICATIVE-CLAUSE — Incorrect clause after be, seem, think, or a similar expression
Student self-check: Check whether the expression requires that, whether/if, a wh-clause, an infinitive, or a noun phrase.
Teacher-facing definition: A clause functioning after a copular or reporting expression is missing or misforms its required complement structure.
Representative incorrect example: The content of this movie is about a man was very poor
Representative correction: The movie is about a man who was very poor

Student-facing error label: Wrong verb form after a modal or auxiliary
Searchable grammar label: verb forms after auxiliaries and modals
Complete literacy code: VERB-AFTER-AUX — Wrong verb form after a modal or auxiliary
Student self-check: Use the base form after do or a modal, the past participle after have, and the required participle/complement after be.
Teacher-facing definition: A modal, do-support, or auxiliary is followed by an inflected form instead of the base/participle form required.
Representative correction: I didn't know how to organise

Complete literacy code: WORD-ORDER — Incorrect English word order
Student self-check: Arrange the subject, verb, object, complements, and adverbs in standard English order for this clause type.
Teacher-facing definition: Adverbs, objects, complements, or question elements are in non-English order.
Representative incorrect example: learn more about the business deeper
Representative correction: learn more deeply about business

Complete literacy code: PRONOUN-EXTRA — Unnecessary pronoun or double subject/object
Student self-check: Remove the pronoun when the noun phrase already fills the same subject or object role.
Teacher-facing definition: A redundant pronoun creates a double subject/object.
Representative incorrect example: thanks to the peers I met, they gave me
Representative correction: the peers I met gave me

Complete literacy code: APPOSITIVE — Incorrect appositive phrase structure
Student self-check: An appositive must rename a nearby noun and attach clearly to it without replacing a required clause element.
Teacher-facing definition: An appositive noun phrase is attached without a valid grammatical relationship to the clause it explains.
Representative correction: a word: 'calm' / the word 'calm'

Student-facing error label: Incorrect coordination with and, or, or but
Searchable grammar label: coordination with and, or and but
Complete literacy code: COORDINATION — Incorrect coordination with and, or, or but
Student self-check: Make the coordinated elements grammatically compatible and ensure shared words apply logically to each item.
Teacher-facing definition: Coordinated elements do not share compatible grammatical structure or scope.
Representative incorrect example: like Jupiter ... and also including the far galaxies
Representative correction: such as Jupiter ... and distant galaxies

Student-facing error label: Pronoun does not agree with its antecedent
Complete literacy code: PRONOUN-AGREEMENT — Pronoun does not agree with its antecedent
Student self-check: Match the pronoun's number and person to the noun it refers to.
Teacher-facing definition: Pronoun number/person does not agree with its antecedent.
Representative correction: those sudden turns lead you / my sudden turns lead me

Complete literacy code: THERE-AGREEMENT — There is/are agreement error
Student self-check: Match is/are or was/were to the following notional subject in a there-construction.
Teacher-facing definition: The verb in a there is/are construction does not agree with the notional subject.
Representative correction: there is nothing

Complete literacy code: CONDITIONAL-STRUCTURE — Incorrect if-clause and result-clause structure
Student self-check: Make sure the condition and result form one complete logical conditional pattern.
Teacher-facing definition: If-clause and result clause are structurally or semantically mismatched.

Complete literacy code: NEGATION — Incorrect negative sentence form
Student self-check: Place not correctly and use do-support or the appropriate auxiliary when the main verb cannot carry negation directly.
Teacher-facing definition: Negative placement, do-support, or negative polarity is malformed.
